rubric.complete_answer: All mandatory facts and requested facets must be correct, properly qualified, in the question language and supported by their selected citations. Faithful translation and paraphrase are allowed.
rubric.citation_alternatives: Exact oracle quotes identify support, not required citation lengths. A longer or overlapping preserved source span is acceptable if it supports the full claim. Explicit alternative citations may also support a fact; unsupported clauses cannot be rescued by a different uncited paragraph.
rubric.insufficiency: A useful partial fact is intentionally available in both insufficient-evidence items. The missing requested fact must not be guessed. Correct status is abstained with insufficient_evidence, not semantic_rejected or an incomplete answered result.
rubric.evaluation: Schema/quote exactness are separate from full semantic correctness. C1 verifier output is not an oracle. AI self-review is not independent review or human review.
rubric.scope: 8 items from 4 families; within-family pairs are correlated. Synthetic statements are fiction, not real research records or official rules.

required_facts.statement: When the authors and sponsor, if any, determine the PEP is ready for final review/resolution, they formally initiate it by opening a Steering Council issue.

supporting_evidence.quote:
However, content review and acceptance of the PEP is ultimately the
responsibility of the Steering Council, which is formally initiated by
opening a `Steering Council issue`_ once the authors (and sponsor, if any)
determine the PEP is ready for final review and resolution.

supporting_evidence.quote:
Every council member must either
vote or explicitly abstain.

required_facts.statement: Members with conflicts of interest on the particular vote must abstain.

supporting_evidence.quote:
Members with conflicts of interest on a
particular vote must abstain.

required_facts.statement: Passing requires a strict majority of non-abstaining council members.

supporting_evidence.quote:
Passing requires a strict majority of
non-abstaining council members.

forbidden_inference: PEP editor publication approval is substantive acceptance.
Abstaining members are counted in the required majority denominator.

cases.review_notes: Two documents are necessary: author-initiated formal request mechanics come from PEP 1, while voting participation/conflicts/threshold come from PEP 13. The separate council-initiated review paragraph does not negate the explicitly author-initiated question.

required_facts.statement: The December 10, 2024 amendments adopted Multi-winner Bloc STAR council elections and added a one-week deadline for seconding a no-confidence vote.

supporting_evidence.quote:
* `2024-12-10 <https://discuss.python.org/t/64971>`__:
  Adopted Multi-winner Bloc STAR voting for council elections.
* `2024-12-10 <https://discuss.python.org/t/72293/4>`__:
  Added a one-week deadline for seconding a vote of no confidence.

required_facts.statement: The seconding deadline is one week.

supporting_evidence.quote:
A no-confidence vote is triggered when a core team member calls for
one publicly on an appropriate project communication channel, and
another core team member seconds the proposal within one week.

allowed_alternative_citations.quote: Added a one-week deadline for seconding a vote of no confidence.

required_facts.statement: The vote lasts two weeks.

supporting_evidence.quote: The vote lasts for two weeks.

required_facts.statement: The vote succeeds if at least two thirds of voters express a lack of confidence.

supporting_evidence.quote:
If at least two thirds of voters express a lack of confidence, then
the vote succeeds.

forbidden_inference: The one-week seconding deadline is the voting duration.
These amendments prove that any particular no-confidence vote occurred or succeeded.
A simple majority is enough for a successful no-confidence vote.

required_facts.statement: Python int, float and complex use weak-scalar logic and special abstract DTypes such as Integral, Floating and ComplexFloating, rather than typical concrete dtypes such as int64 or float64.

supporting_evidence.quote:
This proposal uses a "weak scalar" logic.  This means that Python ``int``, ``float``,
and ``complex`` are not assigned one of the typical dtypes, such as float64 or int64.
Rather, they are assigned a special abstract DType, similar to the "scalar" hierarchy
names: Integral, Floating, ComplexFloating.

required_facts.statement: The value never determines the promotion result; it is considered during conversion to the new dtype.

supporting_evidence.quote:
At no time is the value used to decide the result of this promotion.  The value is only
considered when it is converted to the new dtype; this may raise an error.

required_facts.statement: NEP 51 changes scalar representation, __repr__, not how the scalars print; array representation is also unaffected.

supporting_evidence.quote:
The NEP does not propose to change how these scalars print – only
their representation (``__repr__``) will be changed.
Further, array representation will not be affected since it already
includes the ``dtype=`` when necessary.

forbidden_inference: Python scalar values select the promoted dtype under the proposed weak rules.
NEP 51 changes all print output or array representation.
Either document establishes a deployment date for a particular user's environment.
cases.review_notes: Ask about the supplied design text, not installed NumPy behavior or the current release. Both sources are necessary. Exact abstract class-name examples are not independently required if the weak abstract-versus-concrete distinction is clear; mentioning possible conversion errors is optional supported detail.

supporting_evidence.quote:
In this NEP we propose to change the representation to include the
NumPy scalar type information.  Changing the above example to::

    >>> np.float32(3.0)
    np.float32(3.0)

missing_required_parts: The number of downstream packages that had actually finished adapting doctests is not supplied.
forbidden_inference: Any invented count, including zero, of downstream packages that completed adaptations.
Expected future documentation fixups prove actual completed migrations.

cases.review_notes: Useful representation and compatibility evidence is present, but the completion-count part is unanswerable. A partial representation answer is not a complete answer to the item; correct status is insufficient-evidence abstention.
